mainTopic: Learning the laws of a בכור from במדבר 18:18, how long the owner may keep a בכור בעל מום, and a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its מום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a back-and-forth about the פסוק 'וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ'. רב יהודה in the name of רב and the חכמים of the school of רב argue over which words teach that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night, and which words teach that a בכור בעל מום goes to the כהן. Next the גמרא asks about our משנה: when a בכור gets a מום in its first year, does the owner get any time after the year? A first ברייתא cannot settle it. A second ברייתא gives only enough days after the year to complete thirty days from the מום. In one version this supports רבי אלעזר. In another version רבי אלעזר gives thirty full days after the year, and that version is refuted. A new משנה follows: רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue about a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its מום, and a non-expert who approves a slaughter must pay. רבה בר בר חנה explains that everyone forbids eye blemishes, and they argue only about body blemishes, which רבי מאיר forbids as a גזירה. The amud ends as רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the comparison to breast and thigh is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the other side does not learn the time limit for eating a בכור from the comparison to חזה ושוק. Someone could say the comparison is to the חזה ושוק of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? If you learn it from there, someone could say the comparison is to the breast and thigh of a thanks offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the other side does not learn the rule from the comparison 'like the breast and thigh', and answers right away. It is also setting up the next back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse compares the meat of a בכור to the חזה ושוק. But there are two kinds: the חזה ושוק of שלמים, eaten for two days and one night, and the חזה ושוק of a תודה, eaten for only one day and night. So the comparison alone does not tell us which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? How does the other side explain this?
From there, meaning from that verse or phrase
One could say
The breast and thigh of a קרבן, given to the כהן
Thanks offering, eaten for only one day and night

steps.confusionAlert: 'וְאִידַּךְ' keeps switching sides through this whole section. Each time it means 'what does the OTHER view say to that?' Keep track of whose turn it is.

phrases.english: And the other side?
phrases.notes: This asks: why doesn't the other view learn the rule from that verse?

phrases.english: If it were learned from there, one could say
the breast and thigh of a thanks offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a סוגיא from earlier on the דף, explaining why one side rejects a derivation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why doesn't the other side learn the rule from the comparison to חזה ושוק?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the comparison could point to the חזה ושוק of a תודה, which is eaten for only one day.

steps.title: The extra 'it shall be yours' settles the question
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's side answers: the verse repeats 'לך יהיה', and the extra 'being' gives the בכור extra time, like שלמים and not like תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? The verse says 'It shall be yours.' The verse added another 'being' for the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side answers the problem from step 1. The verse says 'יהיה' a second time, and this extra word shows the comparison is to the longer time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already said 'וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ' and then says 'לְךָ יִהְיֶה' again at the end. That repeated word is read as adding something to the בכור: an extra day. This rules out the תודה reading, which allows only one day.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse added something
'Being', a form of the word יהיה
A firstborn animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: And the other side?
The verse says: "It shall be yours"
the verse added for you
another 'being' regarding a firstborn.
phrases.notes: The word 'יהיה' shows up twice in the verse. The second one adds extra time for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: An extra word in the verse removes the doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison might be to the חזה ושוק of a תודה (one day)
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'יהיה' adds time, so the comparison is to שלמים (two days and one night)

steps.title: The extra words are needed for a blemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of the school of רב answer that 'יהיה לך' is needed for something else. It teaches that a בכור בעל מום is given to the כהן, which the Torah never says anywhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? From there one can say: this 'it shall be yours' teaches about a blemished firstborn, that one gives it to the priest, since we have not found this anywhere in the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side says the extra words cannot be used for the time limit. They are already needed to teach a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יהיה לך' are needed to teach that even a בכור with a מום goes to the כהן. Without these words, we would have no source for that law in the Torah. Since the words are used up on this law, they cannot also prove the time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought as a קרבן
He gives it to the כהן
We have not found it, meaning there is no other source

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the גמרא shows the source that a בכור בעל מום still belongs to the כהן, even though it cannot be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: And the other side?
About that source, one can say:
this "it shall be yours"
teaches about a blemished firstborn
that one gives it to the priest,
since we have not found it
anywhere in the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 2 by using the same words for a different law
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for another law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra 'יהיה' teaches extra eating time
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'יהיה' teaches that a בכור בעל מום goes to the כהן

steps.title: 'Their flesh' covers the blemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's side learns the law of the בכור בעל מום from a different word: the plural 'וּבְשָׂרָם' includes both a תם and a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? The verse said 'and their flesh': both an unblemished one and a blemished one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה's side shows a different source for the blemished בכור. That leaves the extra 'יהיה' free to teach the time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וּבְשָׂרָם' is plural, 'their flesh', so it is read as covering two kinds of בכור: a perfect one and a blemished one. With this source, the extra 'יהיה' is not needed for the blemished law and can still teach the extra eating time.

keyTerms.meaning: And their flesh, a plural word
Perfect, without a blemish
Both this and that

phrases.english: And the other side?
It says: "and their flesh"
phrases.notes: The plural 'their' is the key here: it hints at two kinds of firstborn.

phrases.english: both an unblemished one and a blemished one,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by finding another source for the blemished בכור
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different word in the verse is the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only 'יהיה לך' could teach the law of a blemished בכור
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וּבְשָׂרָם' teaches it, so 'יהיה' is free to teach the time limit

steps.title: 'Their flesh' means the firstborns of all Israel
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of the school of רב say the plural 'וּבְשָׂרָם' does not include blemished animals. It is plural because it means the firstborns of all of כלל ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? 'And their flesh' is said about these firstborns of all of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side explains the plural word another way, so it cannot be a source for blemished firstborns. This is the last move in the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural is needed simply because the verse speaks of everyone's firstborn animals, not one person's. So 'וּבְשָׂרָם' teaches nothing about a בעל מום. For this side, 'יהיה לך' is still needed for the blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Of all of ישראל
It is saying, meaning this is what the verse refers to

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a בכור בעל מום goes to the כהן. They disagree about which words teach it: 'יהיה לך' or 'וּבשרם'. That decides whether the extra 'יהיה' is free to teach that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.

phrases.english: And the other side?
"and their flesh" is about these firstborns
of all the Israelites, it is saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ — ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ דְּהָנֵי בְּכוֹרוֹת דְּכוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns aside the proof in step 4 by reading the plural another way
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another reading of the plural word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural 'וּבְשָׂרָם' includes the blemished בכור
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural refers to the firstborns of all of ישראל, so it says nothing about a בעל מום

steps.title: Do the thirty days come on top of the twelve months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks whether a בכור that got a מום in its first year gets thirty extra days after the year, or whether the thirty days apply only to a מום that appears after the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if a מום appeared during its first year, the owner may keep it the whole twelve months. A question was asked: how should we read this? Does it mean that when the מום appeared within the year he may keep it the twelve months, and then thirty more days after the year? Or does it mean that when the מום appeared within the year he gets the twelve months and nothing more, and when it appeared after the year he may keep it only thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks how to read it. There are two possible readings of how the twelve months and the thirty days fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: the two time limits add up, so a first-year מום gives twelve months plus thirty days. Reading two: they are two separate cases, so a first-year מום gets only the twelve months, and the thirty days are only for a מום that appears after the year.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן
He is allowed to keep it (before giving it to the כהן)
A question was asked among them (an open question)
And nothing more
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree a first-year מום gets the full twelve months. The only question is whether thirty extra days are added after that.

phrases.english: If a blemish developed within its first year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he is permitted to keep it the entire twelve months.
A question was asked before them:
How is it saying this?
If it developed within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: he may keep it the entire twelve months,
and after its year also thirty more days?
Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּנוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: where the blemish developed within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְתוּ לָא,
phrases.english: he may keep it the entire twelve months and no more,
and where it developed after its year,
he may keep it only thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a fresh line of the משנה about how long the owner may keep a בכור בעל מום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a first-year מום gets twelve months plus thirty days, or only twelve months, with the thirty days reserved for a מום that appears after the year.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to give thirty days after the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a בכור nowadays. It gives twelve months for a first-year מום, and then says that after the year the owner may still keep it thirty days. This seems to support the reading that the thirty days come on top of the twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: a בכור nowadays, before it has a מום that can be shown to a חכם, may be kept two or three years. Once it has such a מום, if the מום appeared within its first year, he may keep it the whole twelve months. After its year he may not keep it even one day, even one hour. But because of returning a lost item to its owners, the חכמים said he may keep it thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. The ברייתא seems to give thirty extra days after the year to an animal whose מום appeared in its first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first talks about a מום within the first year and gives twelve months. Then it says 'after the year, thirty days.' This looks like the same animal getting thirty more days, which supports the first reading: the time limits add together.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
To show it to a חכם, an expert who decides if the מום is real
Returning a lost item

steps.whyThisMatters: Nowadays a בכור cannot be brought as a קרבן, so the owner may only use it once it has a real מום. That is why the time limits for keeping it matter.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
A firstborn animal in the present time,
until it is fit to be shown to an expert,
he may keep it two or three years,
and once it is fit to be shown to an expert,
if the blemish developed within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he may keep it the entire twelve months.
After its year he is not permitted to keep it

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: even one day, and even one hour.
But because of returning a lost item to the owners,
they said: he may keep it thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of Step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a first-year מום gets twelve months and then thirty more days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a בכור nowadays that lists twelve months for a first-year מום, then thirty days 'after its year.'

steps.title: The ברייתא has the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the ברייתא is not clear proof. Its thirty days 'after the year' could mean a מום that first appeared after the year, or a מום that appeared before the year ended. So the question remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I can still ask the same question about the ברייתא: are the thirty days for a מום that appeared after the year, or perhaps for one that appeared before the year ended?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The ברייתא's words can be read both ways, just like the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'After its year, thirty days' might be a new case: an animal whose מום appeared only after the year. It might also mean an animal with a first-year מום that has now passed its year. Since both readings fit, the ברייתא does not decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And I can still ask the question
Before its year ended

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives twelve months for a first-year מום and mentions thirty days. The first ברייתא cannot settle whether a first-year מום gets time after the year, because it can be read both ways. The next step brings a clearer ברייתא.

phrases.english: But I can still raise the question:
Are the thirty days for a blemish after its year,
or perhaps for one that came before its year ended?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 7 by showing the ברייתא has the same ambiguity as the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא. The original question remains, and step 9 answers it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's 'after its year, thirty days' can mean either a מום that first appeared after the year or a first-year מום, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא answers the question: the extra days complete thirty from the מום
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a מום appeared fifteen days before the year ended, the owner gets fifteen more days after the year. This totals thirty days from the מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the blemish appeared fifteen days before the end of its year, they give it fifteen more days after its year. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to settle the question from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the owner keep a first-year מום animal past the end of its year, so the second reading ('twelve months and nothing more') is wrong. But it gives only fifteen days after the year, just enough to reach thirty days counted from when the מום appeared. So the thirty days run from the day of the מום, not as a fresh period after the twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: They complete: the owner gets just enough days to fill up a set amount
Learn from it: this proves the point

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ,
phrases.english: If a blemish appeared in it on the fifteenth day within its year,
phrases.notes: He means fifteen days before its first year runs out.

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: they complete for it fifteen days after its year.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed aside in step 8, the גמרא brings a clearer ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether a first-year מום gets thirty days after the year or only enough days to complete thirty from the מום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a מום fifteen days before the year's end gets fifteen days after the year.

steps.title: This ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר, who says the thirty days are counted from when the מום appeared.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, who said: they give him thirty days from the time the blemish appeared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא it just quoted backs up a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר counts the thirty days from the day of the מום. The ברייתא's 'fifteen plus fifteen' fits that exactly. So רבי אלעזר's ruling and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports: a source that backs up an Amora's view
From the time the blemish appeared

phrases.english: This supports רבי אלעזר,
as רבי אלעזר said:
They give him thirty days
from the time the blemish appeared in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the ברייתא from step 9 to an אמורא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the thirty days are counted from the appearance of the מום.

steps.title: A second version: רבי אלעזר gives thirty full days after the year
steps.stepSummary: Others report רבי אלעזר differently. In their version, a first-year מום gets thirty days after the year. He learns this from 'שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה', since thirty days can count as a 'year'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי אלעזר said: From where do we know that a בכור that got a מום within its year gets thirty days after its year? The פסוק says: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year.' Which days count as a year? You must say: thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what רבי אלעזר said. Here his ruling is the opposite of what the ברייתא seemed to say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the thirty days come on top of the twelve months, not counted from the מום. The source is the double wording 'שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה': it means one year and then a bit more. Thirty days are treated as an important part of a year, so they count as the second 'שָׁנָה'.

keyTerms.meaning: From where: asking for a source in the פסוקים
Year by year: the words of the פסוק about eating the בכור
Days that count as a year

steps.confusionAlert: Watch out: this is a second report of what רבי אלעזר said. The step 10 version and this version disagree about when the thirty days start.

phrases.english: There are those who say: רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִבְכוֹר שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ
phrases.english: From where do we know that a firstborn which got a blemish within its year

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ?
phrases.english: is given thirty days after its year?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״,
phrases.english: As it says: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year.'
Which are the days that count as a year?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; read the word in square brackets, 'אֵילּוּ', instead.

phrases.english: You must say: these are thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי אלעזר's view, which takes the opposite side of the question from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור that got a מום within its first year gets thirty full days after the year, learned from 'שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה'.

steps.title: The same ברייתא challenges this version of רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only completes thirty days from the מום (fifteen after the year). That shows there is no full extra thirty days, which goes against the second version of רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: if a blemish appeared fifteen days before the end of its year, they complete fifteen days after its year. Completing, yes; giving a full thirty, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבי אלעזר, using the same ברייתא that supported the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's word is 'completing'. The owner only gets enough days to reach thirty from the מום. He does not get a brand-new thirty days after the year, which is exactly what the second version of רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: Completing: filling up to the thirty days
Giving: granting a whole new period

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד לוֹ מוּם בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ —
phrases.english: If a blemish appeared in it on the fifteenth day within its year,

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם אַחַר שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: they complete for it fifteen days after its year.
Completing: yes.
Giving: no!
phrases.notes: He means giving a whole new thirty days after the year, which is what רבי אלעזר said in step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רבי אלעזר from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבי אלעזר: thirty full days after the year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא only completes thirty days from the מום. It does not grant a full thirty after the year.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר is refuted in this version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the second version of רבי אלעזר is truly refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רבי אלעזר; it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final word: the challenge stands, and the second version of רבי אלעזר is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered for רבי אלעזר, so the ברייתא wins. In this version his view is rejected: a first-year מום gets only enough days to complete thirty from the מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: an Amora's view is disproved by a תנאי source

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא counts the thirty days from when the מום appeared. In the first version this supports רבי אלעזר. In the second version, where he gives thirty days after the year, it refutes him.

phrases.english: The refutation of רבי אלעזר is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 12 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The thirty days are counted from when the מום appears. There is no full thirty days added after the year.

steps.title: New משנה: a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its מום
steps.stepSummary: Someone slaughtered a בכור and only afterward showed its מום to an expert. רבי יהודה permits it. רבי מאיר forbids it, because it was not slaughtered on an expert's approval.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters the בכור and then shows its blemish: רבי יהודה permits it. רבי מאיר says: since it was slaughtered without an expert's approval, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It has a disagreement about a בכור that was slaughtered before an expert approved its מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the מום turns out to be real. The only problem is the order: slaughter came first, and the expert came later. רבי יהודה looks at the result, so he permits it. רבי מאיר says the expert's approval must come before the slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
An expert who is qualified to judge blemishes
Based on someone's ruling
Permits

phrases.english: משנה: One who slaughters the firstborn
and then shows its blemish:
רבי יהודה permits it.
רבי מאיר says:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְנִשְׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי מוּמְחֶה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered not on an expert's ruling, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וּמַרְאֶה אֶת מוּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits a בכור slaughtered before an expert saw its מום; רבי מאיר forbids it.

steps.title: A non-expert who approves a בכור must pay
steps.stepSummary: If a non-expert examined a בכור and it was slaughtered because of his ruling, the animal must be buried, and he must pay from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone who is not an expert looks at the בכור, and it is slaughtered on his word, it must be buried, and he must pay from his own pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case: a non-expert who ruled that a בכור could be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the approval came from someone without the right to give it, the meat cannot be used and must be buried. The non-expert caused the loss, so he pays for it from his own property.

keyTerms.meaning: It must be buried: the meat is forbidden
He must pay from his own property

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר,
phrases.english: One who is not an expert and examines the firstborn,
and it is slaughtered on his word:
this animal must be buried,
and he must pay from his own property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה: a non-expert who approved the slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור slaughtered on a non-expert's ruling is buried, and the non-expert pays from his own property.

steps.title: Eye blemishes are forbidden by all; the argument is only about body blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה limits the מחלוקת. Everyone forbids eye blemishes. רבי מאיר forbids body blemishes as a גזירה, and רבי יהודה permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה says: with blemishes on the eye, everyone agrees the animal is forbidden, because they change. They argue only about blemishes on the body. רבי מאיר holds we make a decree forbidding body blemishes because of eye blemishes. רבי יהודה holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by narrowing down exactly where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An eye blemish can change after death, so an expert looking at it afterward cannot tell whether it was a permanent מום. A body blemish does not change, so the only question is whether to forbid it anyway as a גזירה, so that people do not confuse it with eye blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Blemishes on the cornea of the eye
Blemishes on the body
They change (after the animal dies)
We make a decree on one case because of another
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not say body blemishes change. He forbids them only as a גזירה, because of the eye blemishes, which do change.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the frame for the whole סוגיא: one case is forbidden because the facts cannot be checked, and the other is forbidden only as a protective גזירה.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba bar bar Chana says:
With blemishes on the cornea of the eye,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden,
because they change.
phrases.notes: He means they change after death, so an expert can no longer tell if the blemish was permanent.

phrases.english: They disagreed only about blemishes on the body,
for Rabbi Meir holds:

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרִינַן מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף אַטּוּ דּוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן,
phrases.english: we decree against body blemishes because of eye blemishes,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא גָּזְרִינַן מוּמִין שֶׁבַּגּוּף אַטּוּ דּוּקִּין שֶׁבָּעַיִן.
phrases.english: we do not decree against body blemishes because of eye blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eye blemishes are forbidden by everyone. Body blemishes are forbidden by רבי מאיר as a גזירה and permitted by רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה forbidding eye blemishes and permitting body blemishes, while רבי מאיר forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught: if someone slaughters a בכור and afterward shows its blemishes, רבי יהודה says eye blemishes are forbidden because they change, and body blemishes are permitted because they do not change. רבי מאיר says both are forbidden, because they change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches what רבה בר בר חנה just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states outright that רבי יהודה also forbids eye blemishes, so the argument is only about body blemishes. That is exactly רבה בר בר חנה's point. However, רבי מאיר's reason, 'because they change,' sounds odd for body blemishes, and the next step picks up on that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)
One who slaughters
Shows its blemishes (to an expert)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: It is also taught so:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּכוֹר וּמַרְאֶה אֶת מוּמָיו —
phrases.english: One who slaughters the firstborn and then shows its blemishes,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
with eye blemishes it is forbidden,
because they change;
with body blemishes it is permitted,
because they do not change.
Rabbi Meir says:
both this and that are forbidden,
because they change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר בר חנה's statement from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that eye blemishes are forbidden by all, and the argument is only about body blemishes
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר on a בכור shown to an expert after slaughter

steps.title: Do body blemishes really change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's wording, since body blemishes do not change after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you think the reason is 'because they change'? Do body blemishes change?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי מאיר's reason in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יהודה said body blemishes do not change, and that is simply true. So רבי מאיר cannot mean that body blemishes themselves change. The wording needs to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)
Do...? (a question word)

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind that it is 'because they change'?
Do body blemishes change?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason given for רבי מאיר in the ברייתא of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'מפני שהן משתנין' said about both kinds of blemishes in רבי מאיר's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Body blemishes plainly do not change after death, so that cannot be the reason for forbidding them.

steps.title: Read it as: because of the ones that change
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording is fixed: body blemishes are forbidden because of the eye blemishes, which change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: because of the ones that change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading רבי מאיר's reason in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one word turns 'because they change' into 'because of the ones that change.' Now רבי מאיר forbids body blemishes as a גזירה because of eye blemishes. This matches רבה בר בר חנה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the corrected reading)
Because of the ones that change

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone forbids eye blemishes, because they change after death. רבי מאיר also forbids body blemishes, but only as a גזירה because of the eye blemishes. רבי יהודה permits body blemishes.

phrases.english: Rather: because of the ones that change.
phrases.notes: The ones that change are the eye blemishes. Body blemishes are forbidden only so people will not mix them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seemed to say that body blemishes themselves change.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר forbids body blemishes because of eye blemishes, which change. This is a גזירה, as רבה בר בר חנה said.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement from רב נחמן בר יצחק, which continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It opens a new statement from רב נחמן בר יצחק, and the content of that statement comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the speaker appears here. His actual point follows right after, so wait for it before drawing any conclusions.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new statement after the ברייתא's wording has been settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated here; this line only introduces רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement, which follows.
